question:
A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, fatigue, and
a dry cough. She mentions that her symptoms have been gradually worsening, and she has difficulty
breathing when lying flat on her back. She reports no recent travel or exposure to illness. Medical
history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination reveals
diminished breath sounds bilaterally, fine inspiratory crackles at lung bases, and an increased
respiratory rate. A chest radiograph shows bilateral diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Which of the following
techniques is most appropriate for decreasing sympathetic activity to improve recovery in this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Craniosacral therapy (B) HVLA (High-Velocity Low-Amplitude) to the thoracic
spine (C) Thoracoabdominal diaphragm release (D) Diaphragmatic doming (E) Rib raising (F)
Suboccipital release (G) Thoracic lymphatic pump (H) Myofascial release of the thoracic inlet (I)
Thoracic inlet release (J) Counterstrain of the cervical spine
 A. Thoracoabdominal diaphragm release
B. HVLA (High-Velocity Low-Amplitude) to the thoracic spine
C. Suboccipital release
D. Counterstrain of the cervical spine
E. Thoracic inlet release
F. Craniosacral therapy
G. Rib raising
H. Diaphragmatic doming
I. Myofascial release of the thoracic inlet
J. Thoracic lymphatic pump
